record.original_question: In the setting where a Lie group G acts on the space 𝓜 of holomorphic maps from a homogeneous complex manifold M to Pn, extend Benjamin Weiss’s construction of non-trivial invariant probability measures to this broader action.

evidence.quote: Recently, Benjamin Weiss has proved the existence of non-trivial probability measures on H which are invariant by the above translation operator, see [30].

Problem 9.3. Consider a complex manifold M of dimension n which is homogeneous under the action of a Lie group G. Let M denote the space of holomorphic maps from M to Pn, endowed with the topology of uniform convergence on compact sets. The group G acts on this space. (ii) Extend the construction by B. Weiss to this context.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a Lie group acting transitively and holomorphically on a complex manifold $M$ of complex dimension $n$, so that $M$ is homogeneous under $G$. Let $\mathbb{P}^n$ denote complex projective space of dimension $n$, and let $\mathcal{M} = \mathrm{Hol}(M, \mathbb{P}^n)$ be the space of holomorphic maps from $M$ to $\mathbb{P}^n$, equipped with the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets of $M$. The group $G$ acts continuously on $\mathcal{M}$ by precomposition: for $g \in G$ and $f \in \mathcal{M}$, $(g \cdot f)(z) = f(g^{-1} \cdot z)$.

A classical result of B. Weiss asserts that on the space $\mathcal{H}$ of entire functions $\mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, equipped with the topology of uniform convergence on compact sets, there exist non-trivial Borel probability measures invariant under the action of the translation group $\mathbb{C}$ (i.e., measures not supported on constant functions).

Problem: Construct a non-trivial $G$-invariant Borel probability measure on $\mathcal{M}$, that is, a Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathcal{M}$ such that $\mu(g \cdot A) = \mu(A)$ for every $g \in G$ and every Borel set $A \subseteq \mathcal{M}$, and such that $\mu$ is not supported on the set of constant maps. Equivalently, extend Weiss's construction of non-trivial invariant probability measures from the case of entire functions under translation to this general homogeneous setting.
artifact.category_tag: Invariant measures on spaces of holomorphic maps
artifact.status_search_result: Weiss's original construction of non-trivial translation-invariant probability measures on the space of entire functions on $\mathbb{C}$ has been studied and refined by Buhovsky, Glücksam, Logunov, and Sodin (J. d'Analyse Math., 2019; arXiv:1703.08101), and extensions have been investigated for harmonic functions on $\mathbb{R}^2$. However, no source was found establishing the general extension to spaces of holomorphic maps from an arbitrary homogeneous complex manifold $M$ to $\mathbb{P}^n$ under a transitive Lie group action; the status of this general problem appears unverified.

status_evidence.title: Translation-invariant probability measures on entire functions
status_evidence.snippet: We study non-trivial translation-invariant probability measures on the space of entire functions of one complex variable... existence (and even an abundance) of such measures was proven by B. Weiss.
status_evidence.claim: Weiss's construction in the classical case of entire functions has been studied and partially extended (growth bounds, harmonic functions), but a generalization to holomorphic maps from arbitrary homogeneous complex manifolds to projective space is not established.

status_evidence.title: Translation-invariant probability measures on harmonic functions (seminar)
status_evidence.snippet: Probability measures on the space of harmonic functions on R^2, which are invariant with respect to translations and are not supported on constant functions; a wild object introduced by B. Weiss.
status_evidence.claim: Extensions of Weiss's construction exist for harmonic functions on R^2, but the general homogeneous Lie group setting is not addressed.
